questions.q: What is a Microsoft Sentinel playbook, technically?
options: A real Azure Logic App, created and run inside the separate Azure Logic Apps service
A Sentinel-only automation engine with no relationship to any other Azure service
A PowerShell script stored inside the Log Analytics workspace
A KQL query that runs on a schedule
questions.explain: Sentinel doesn't host its own workflow engine — a playbook is a genuine Azure Logic App, using a connector to read from and act on Sentinel.

questions.q: What are the three building blocks every Azure Logic App workflow is made of?
options: Trigger, connectors, and actions
Tables, queries, and dashboards
Incidents, alerts, and bookmarks
Workspaces, connectors, and retention policies
questions.explain: A trigger starts the workflow, connectors are pre-built integrations to other systems, and actions are the steps that run after the trigger fires.

questions.q: How many triggers does a single Logic App workflow have?
options: Exactly one, and it always runs first
As many as the designer allows, running in any order
Zero — workflows start manually every time
One per connector used in the workflow
questions.explain: Every workflow has exactly one trigger, and it's always first; everything after it is an action.

questions.q: What does the Microsoft Sentinel connector expose to a Logic App?
options: A trigger for incident creation/update, plus actions like getting incident details or adding a comment/tag
Only the ability to run KQL queries against Log Analytics
A way to provision new Azure virtual machines
Nothing — Sentinel playbooks don't use connectors at all
questions.explain: The Microsoft Sentinel connector is built for this exact job: trigger on incident created/updated, plus actions to read and write back to that incident.

questions.q: In the playbook shape TRIGGER -> Get incident details -> Post to Teams -> Add a tag, what does each action line name?
options: The connector it's calling
The KQL table it queries
The analyst assigned to the incident
The Azure region the action runs in
questions.explain: Each action names its connector (Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Teams, etc.), which is what makes a playbook's shape readable at a glance.
